papers.title: pyGENIE: A Python library for programmatic access and mutational analysis of AACR Project GENIE
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation As of today, AACR Project GENIE has completed 19 data releases since its launch in 2015. The latest release includes more than 268 000 samples from nearly 250 000 patients, and as of February 2026, over 1730 scientific journal articles have cited Project GENIE data. Despite its scale and scientific impact, programmatic analysis of GENIE data often still requires researchers to work directly with complex flat files and develop custom data integration workflows. Results Here we present pyGENIE, a Python package that provides a unified API for accessing GENIE flat files, performing clinical and genomic queries, computing tumor mutational burden, and integrating with leading mutational signature analysis tools including SigProfiler and SigMA. Following a data-as-a-service paradigm, pyGENIE returns all results as native pandas DataFrames, enabling seamless integration with machine learning and visualization libraries. Applied to a lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) case study, pyGENIE reproduces known mutation frequencies, co-mutation patterns, and mutational signatures while reducing the required codebase by approximately an order of magnitude. papers.title: RNAcomp2D: a web tool to execute multiple methods and visually compare predictions of RNA secondary structure
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Ribonucleic acids (RNAs) are involved in many important biological processes. In particular, non-coding RNAs are crucial regulators of cellular processes, playing a significant role in gene expression. RNA secondary structure is key to infer their specific function and for understanding how they interact with other molecules. Many computational models have been developed in the last decade to predict the secondary structure, achieving increasingly higher success rates. However, each new method has its own input-output interface, programming language, computational requirements and, sometimes, a dedicated server to run the model or just a source code in a repository. Thus, nowadays it is very hard to obtain predictions from multiple methods and compare them at once. A unified interface is urgently needed, which allows accessing several methods at the same time, visualizing and comparing predictions among them, and also with a reference structure when available. Results We introduce here RNAcomp2D, a web-based tool that allows users to enter an RNA sequence, or select one from RNAcentral, and obtain predictions of RNA secondary structures using several state-of-the-art methods. Both classical thermodynamic methods and the latest deep learning models are packaged in containers and accessible in an unified website. All the predictions, and the reference structure if available, are shown at the same time in a single graphical interface. Moreover, as new models continue to be developed, this tool is designed to be scalable, allowing the addition of more prediction methods in the future. Availability Web server is available at https://sinc.unl.edu.ar/web-demo/rnacomp2d/ . Data and source code are available at https://github.com/sinc-lab/RNAcomp2D

papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Ribonucleic acids (RNAs) are involved in many important biological processes. In particular, non-coding RNAs are crucial regulators of cellular processes, playing a significant role in gene expression. RNA secondary structure is key to infer their specific function and for understanding how they interact with other molecules. Many computational models have been developed in the last decade to predict the secondary structure, achieving increasingly higher success rates. However, each new method has its own input-output interface, programming language, computational requirements and, sometimes, a dedicated server to run the model or just a source code in a repository. Thus, nowadays it is very hard to obtain predictions from multiple methods and compare them at once. A unified interface is urgently needed, which allows accessing several methods at the same time, visualizing and comparing predictions among them, and also with a reference structure when available.

RESULTS: We introduce here RNAcomp2D, a web-based tool that allows users to enter an RNA sequence, or select one from RNAcentral, and obtain predictions of RNA secondary structures using several state-of-the-art methods. Both classical thermodynamic methods and the latest deep learning models are packaged in containers and accessible in an unified website. All the predictions, and the reference structure if available, are shown at the same time in a single graphical interface. Moreover, as new models continue to be developed, this tool is designed to be scalable, allowing the addition of more prediction methods in the future.

AVAILABILITY: Web server is available at https://sinc.unl.edu.ar/web-demo/rnacomp2d/. Data and source code are available at https://github.com/sinc-lab/RNAcomp2D.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.title: ABAQS: A comprehensive scoring method for assessing genome annotation quality
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation As genome resources continue to expand, estimating the accuracy and completeness of genome annotations (e.g., gene and protein models) becomes essential to ensure quality of downstream analyses and applications. It becomes critical in comparative genomic analysis to select genomes with comparable qualities of assembly and annotation. Without careful scrutiny, inconsistencies in annotation quality can undermine downstream studies. Results We have developed Accuracy-Based Annotation Quality Score (ABAQS), a novel method to comprehensively assess genome annotation quality. ABAQS evaluates multiple factors, including genome completeness, gene model validity, and protein profile accuracy, providing a more complete picture of annotation quality than metrics like BUSCO and PSAURON. We applied ABAQS to 1700+ eukaryotic fungal and algal genomes and showed its robustness and effectiveness in evaluating genome annotation quality, making it a valuable tool for researchers working with genomic data. Availability ABAQS software is available at https://github.com/mycocosm-lbl/abaqs . It requires Java SDK version > =21 and Maven. We also provide a Docker image on DockerHub

all_papers.title: pyGENIE: A Python library for programmatic access and mutational analysis of AACR Project GENIE
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation As of today, AACR Project GENIE has completed 19 data releases since its launch in 2015. The latest release includes more than 268 000 samples from nearly 250 000 patients, and as of February 2026, over 1730 scientific journal articles have cited Project GENIE data. Despite its scale and scientific impact, programmatic analysis of GENIE data often still requires researchers to work directly with complex flat files and develop custom data integration workflows. Results Here we present pyGENIE, a Python package that provides a unified API for accessing GENIE flat files, performing clinical and genomic queries, computing tumor mutational burden, and integrating with leading mutational signature analysis tools including SigProfiler and SigMA. Following a data-as-a-service paradigm, pyGENIE returns all results as native pandas DataFrames, enabling seamless integration with machine learning and visualization libraries. Applied to a lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) case study, pyGENIE reproduces known mutation frequencies, co-mutation patterns, and mutational signatures while reducing the required codebase by approximately an order of magnitude. Availability pyGENIE is freely available at https://github.com/gersteinlab/pyGENIE under the MIT License, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21981945 , and can be installed from PyPI using pip install pygenie-sdk

all_papers.title: ABAQS: A comprehensive scoring method for assessing genome annotation quality
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation As genome resources continue to expand, estimating the accuracy and completeness of genome annotations (e.g., gene and protein models) becomes essential to ensure quality of downstream analyses and applications. It becomes critical in comparative genomic analysis to select genomes with comparable qualities of assembly and annotation. Without careful scrutiny, inconsistencies in annotation quality can undermine downstream studies. Results We have developed Accuracy-Based Annotation Quality Score (ABAQS), a novel method to comprehensively assess genome annotation quality. ABAQS evaluates multiple factors, including genome completeness, gene model validity, and protein profile accuracy, providing a more complete picture of annotation quality than metrics like BUSCO and PSAURON. We applied ABAQS to 1700+ eukaryotic fungal and algal genomes and showed its robustness and effectiveness in evaluating genome annotation quality, making it a valuable tool for researchers working with genomic data. Availability ABAQS software is available at https://github.com/mycocosm-lbl/abaqs . It requires Java SDK version > =21 and Maven. We also provide a Docker image on DockerHub
